docs.title: MaRDMO Plugin
docs.text:
MaRDMO Logo by MaRDI, licensed under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

MaRDMO is a plugin for the Research Data Management Organiser (RDMO), developed within the Mathematical Research Data Initiative (MaRDI). It enables structured documentation and search of mathematical research artifacts through guided questionnaire interviews. Completed documentations can be exported directly to the MaRDI knowledge graph; existing entries can be queried from the MaRDI Portal, MathModDB, or MathAlgoDB and imported back into RDMO.

docs.title: Catalogs
docs.text:
MaRDMO provides five catalogs:

Catalog Description Algorithm Document algorithms, algorithmic tasks, implementing software, benchmarks, and publications. Based on the MathAlgoDB ontology. Interdisciplinary Workflow Document workflows, process steps, mathematical models, methods, software, hardware, experimental devices, data sets, and publications. Based on the MaRDI standardised scheme (to some extent on the Metadata4Engineering (M4E) ontology). Mathematical Model (detailed) Document models, mathematical formulations, quantities, quantity kinds, computational tasks, research problems, academic disciplines, and publications. Based on the MathModDB ontology. Mathematical Model (basic) Reduced-scope model documentation using the same MathModDB ontology. Search Query existing entries across the MaRDI Portal, MathModDB, and MathAlgoDB knowledge graphs. Results are displayed directly in RDMO.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: MaRDMO requires Python 3.10 or later and RDMO 2.5.1 or later. Follow the installation / update instructions of RDMO if required.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Go to the rdmo-app directory of your RDMO installation. In the virtual environment of the RDMO installation install the MaRDMO Plugin:

pip install MaRDMO

To connect the MaRDMO Plugin with the RDMO installation add the following lines to config/settings/local.py (if not already present):

from django.utils.translation import gettext_lazy as _
from MaRDMO.optionsets import OPTIONSET_PROVIDERS as MARDMO_OPTIONSET_PROVIDERS

INSTALLED_APPS = ['MaRDMO'] + INSTALLED_APPS

PROJECT_EXPORTS += [
        ('wikibase', _('Export to MaRDI Portal'), 'MaRDMO.main.MaRDMOExportProvider'),
        ('wikibase-search', _('Query MaRDI Portal'), 'MaRDMO.main.MaRDMOQueryProvider'),
        ]

# All option set providers of MaRDMO (the questionnaire's option sets name them by key)
OPTIONSET_PROVIDERS += MARDMO_OPTIONSET_PROVIDERS

Up to MaRDMO 0.6 the settings listed the providers one by one (MaRDMO.model.providers.MathematicalModel and so on); these classes no longer exist, so replace such a list by the import and the line OPTIONSET_PROVIDERS += MARDMO_OPTIONSET_PROVIDERS above. Providers of later MaRDMO versions then need no change of the settings.

In addition add the following urlpattern to config/urls.py:

path('services/', include("MaRDMO.urls")),

Thereby, the MaRDMO Plugin is installed and "Export to MaRDI Portal" and "Query MaRDI Portal" buttons are added in the project view.

docs.title: Portal Connection
docs.text:
Add the following lines to config/settings/local.py to connect MaRDMO with the individual databases.

MARDMO_PROVIDER = {
    'mardi': {
        'items': 'data/items.json',
        'properties': 'data/properties.json',
        'api': 'https://portal.mardi4nfdi.de/w/api.php',
        'sparql': 'https://query.portal.mardi4nfdi.de/sparql',
        'uri': 'https://portal.mardi4nfdi.de',
        'entity_uri': 'http://portal.mardi4nfdi.de',
        'oauth2_client_id': '',
        'oauth2_client_secret': '',
    }
}

Contact the MaRDI consortium for the individual credentials. Wikidata needs no configuration; its endpoints are built into MaRDMO.

Formulas entered in the questionnaires are checked with the TeX checker of the MaRDI Portal before the export, so the RDMO server needs to be able to reach the MaRDI Portal. No credentials are needed for this check.

docs.title: Questionnaire Import
docs.text:
The MaRDMO Plugin requires the MaRDMO-Questionnaire, download its latest release .

Integrate the MaRDMO Questionnaire into your RDMO instance through the user interface of your RDMO instance (Management -> Import -> attributes.xml/optionsets.xml/conditions.xml/catalogs.xml) or via 

python manage.py import /path/to/MaRDMO-Questionnaire/catalog/attributes.xml
python manage.py import /path/to/MaRDMO-Questionnaire/catalog/optionsets.xml
python manage.py import /path/to/MaRDMO-Questionnaire/catalog/conditions.xml
python manage.py import /path/to/MaRDMO-Questionnaire/catalog/mardmo-search-catalog.xml
python manage.py import /path/to/MaRDMO-Questionnaire/catalog/mardmo-model-catalog.xml
python manage.py import /path/to/MaRDMO-Questionnaire/catalog/mardmo-model-basics-catalog.xml
python manage.py import /path/to/MaRDMO-Questionnaire/catalog/mardmo-interdisciplinary-workflow-catalog.xml
python manage.py import /path/to/MaRDMO-Questionnaire/catalog/mardmo-algorithm-catalog.xml

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. In RDMO, select Create New Project, enter a project name, and assign one of the five MaRDMO catalogs.
  2. Select Answer Questions to work through the guided interview.
  3. Once complete, return to the project page and use the Export to MaRDI Portal button (for documentation catalogs) or Query MaRDI Portal button (for the search catalog) in the Export section on the right-hand side.

Demo videos are available for model documentation and algorithm documentation.

docs.title: Export Pipeline
docs.text: Clicking "Export to MaRDI Portal" on an RDMO project page triggers a two-phase pipeline. The first click renders a documentation preview; the second click (on the button at the bottom of the preview) performs the authenticated upload. This page walks through every step in order.

docs.title: 1. Catalog Check
docs.text: render() looks up the active project catalog in the template map. If the catalog is not one of the supported MaRDMO catalogs, an error page is returned immediately.

docs.title: 2. Collecting Answers
docs.text:
get_post_data('preview') reads all RDMO project values and assembles them into a nested answers dict via process_question_dict(), organised by entity type (e.g. {"model": {...}, "formulation": {...}, "publication": {...}}).

In preview mode, publication metadata is additionally fetched and merged into the answers dict, and prepare.preview() pre-processes the data into display-ready structures for the template (e.g. paired algorithm–software entries, model–task pairs).

Publications taken from Wikidata or entered by the user are looked up by their DOI (MaRDI Portal, Wikidata, Crossref, DataCite, zbMATH, doi.org, ORCID). Up to three publications are looked up at the same time, and the result for a DOI is kept in Django's cache for an hour, so clicking the preview again does not repeat the lookups. A result is only kept if the MaRDI Portal and Wikidata answered and some source knows the publication; otherwise the next preview looks it up again.

docs.title: 3. Preview
docs.text:
The answers dict is passed to the catalog-appropriate Django template, which renders an HTML documentation preview — a human-readable rendering of everything the user has entered in the questionnaire. Missing fields and invalid values (URLs, DOIs, swMATH IDs, numbers, …) are already flagged with red text at this stage, using the same rules as the checks and the export (see Validation), giving the user a chance to review and correct the documentation before committing to the export. For model catalogs, every formula is checked with the MaRDI Portal's TeX checker; rejected formulas are shown as raw TeX with an explanation. A second "Export to MaRDI Portal" button at the bottom of the preview page triggers the actual export.

Publications are shown as the export writes them: a citation line built from the parts that are known (authors, year, title, journal, volume, issue, pages), what the export creates on the MaRDI Portal (the publication, its journal, new authors), and, in a collapsible Authors and journal section, every author and the journal with its status (on the MaRDI Portal, new, or name only) and its identifiers (ORCiD, zbMath, Wikidata, ISSN).

docs.title: 4. Credential Check
docs.text: submit() checks that oauth2_client_id and oauth2_client_secret are present in the Django settings. If either is missing, an error page is returned before any data processing happens.

docs.title: 5. Validation Checks
docs.text: get_post_data() re-collects the answers dict (submit mode — without publication retrieval). Checks.run_X() then validates the collected answers for completeness and consistency, including the value formats described in Validation and, for the detailed model catalog, the formula check against the MaRDI Portal's TeX checker. In addition, for every entity that would be newly created on the MaRDI Portal, a request is sent to check whether an item with the same label and description combination already exists. If any check fails, a readable error list is returned and the export is aborted.

docs.title: 6. Payload Construction
docs.text:
PrepareX().export() translates the answers dict into a Wikibase-ready payload dict and a dependency graph:

  • unique_items() deduplicates all entities referenced across the questionnaire.
  • process_items() assigns each unique item to one of two tracks:
    • Items already on the MaRDI Portal (mardi: prefix) are registered with their real QID.
    • All other items (from Wikidata, or newly defined) are again checked against the MaRDI Portal for duplicates (_check_mardi_and_raise), then registered as new with an empty QID and a seed list of statements (Wikidata QID, ORCiD, zbMath code, or ISSN as appropriate). The searches for all new items run first, four at a time; a search that still fails after its retries finds nothing, and the MaRDI Portal itself rejects an item whose label and description exist already (see below).

  • add_answer() calls accumulate statements:

    • For new items: statements are appended to the item's payload and will be created together with the item in a single API call.
    • For existing items: each statement becomes a separate RELATION<n> entry that will be posted individually.

    Values are normalised on the way: tabs and outer whitespace are removed from text, formulas are put on one line, and quantity amounts lose leading zeros (see Validation). - Final check: validate_identifiers() checks every URL, DOI, swMATH ID, date and quantity amount in the payload. If any of them would be rejected by the MaRDI Portal, the export is aborted with a list of the affected values before anything is posted. - Relation existence check: build_relation_check_queries() generates SPARQL queries (in chunks of 50 relations) that check, for every RELATION entry targeting an existing item, whether the statement with its qualifiers already exists on the MaRDI Portal. For math-datatype statements a separate API-based check is used, because SPARQL returns MathML while the MaRDI Portal stores LaTeX. If a check cannot be completed, the export is aborted, since posting without it could create duplicate statements. - Qualifier merge: merge_qualifiers() then decides, with the statements of the existing items (fetched via wbgetentities, 50 items per request, shared with the math check), what happens with each RELATION entry (see below): it exists already and is skipped, it is a new statement, or it exists and only gets the qualifiers it lacks.

All requests of these checks (duplicate search, relation and math check, statements for the qualifier merge) are retried twice on a timeout, a connection error, or the answers 429, 502, 503 and 504, after 2 and 5 seconds or the portal's Retry-After (at most 10 seconds); other answers, such as 400, are not retried. Each check gives up after 2 minutes in total. The rule is the one of queries.request_with_retry(), which also retries SPARQL queries and the TeX check once (see Handlers). - Dependency graph: whenever a new item's statement references another new item (identified by an Item<n> placeholder), that dependency is recorded so that items can be created in the correct order.

docs.title: Qualifier Merge
docs.text:
Qualifiers are of two kinds:

  • Meaning qualifiers make a statement what it is: object has role (e.g. a formula contained as initial condition), symbol represents (the quantity of a symbol in a defining formula) and platform (the software and hardware of a workflow usage). The same subject, property and object with another value of these, or without any, is a statement of its own.
  • Additive qualifiers add information to a statement: assumptions, comments, documentation, parameters, years, numbers, and all others.

A RELATION entry is the same as a statement on the MaRDI Portal if subject, property, object and meaning agree. Then:

Portal statement Result has all qualifiers of the entry skipped (exists) lacks some additive qualifiers only these qualifiers are added to it (partial) has another meaning, or none exists a new statement is written

Meaning is compared as follows:

  • No role matches no role only: a plain contains F is written next to contains F as initial condition.
  • A role of the entry that is among the roles of a portal statement matches it: a statement as initial value and parameter is also the one as parameter. MaRDMO writes one role per statement and imports such a statement as one relation for each role the questionnaire offers.
  • Platform and symbol represents must be the same: software and hardware together describe one usage, and its parameters belong to that usage.

Symbols of formulas (in defining formula) are compared with the statements of the same formula or quantity on the MaRDI Portal (check_symbols()), since a symbol stands for exactly one quantity:

Same symbol on the portal Result with the same quantity skipped (exists) with another quantity the export stops: MaRDMO cannot change what the symbol stands for (e.g. a symbol block of a fetched formula deleted and added again with another quantity) without a quantity (no symbol represents) the quantity is added to it (partial) none a new statement is written

The SPARQL check also finds a portal statement with a role for an entry without one, so entries of the properties MaRDMO writes with meaning qualifiers (contains, described by source, uses) are always compared with the portal statements again. Several entries adding to the same statement share it; each qualifier is added once.

docs.title: 7. Cyclic Dependency Check
docs.text: is_cyclic(dependency) inspects the dependency graph before proceeding. If a cycle is detected an error page is returned.

docs.title: 8. OAuth2 Authentication
docs.text: post() serialises the payload and the topological item order into the Django session and redirects the user to the MaRDI Portal OAuth2 authorisation endpoint. After the user approves the access, the portal redirects back to the MaRDMO callback URL. callback() validates the CSRF state token, exchanges the authorisation code for an access token, and launches the background upload.

docs.title: 9. Background Upload
docs.text:
The upload runs in a daemon thread so the browser can display a live progress page immediately. Progress and results are kept in Django's cache, so the progress page works regardless of which server process handles the request. The upload proceeds in two phases:

Phase 1 — New items (in topological dependency order): Each new item is posted to the Wikibase REST API as a single request containing its label, description, aliases, and all its statements at once. Once the MaRDI Portal assigns a real QID, every remaining Item<n> placeholder in the payload is replaced with that QID, so subsequent items that depend on it reference the correct identifier.

Phase 2 — Relations: RELATION<n> entries (statements targeting existing items) and ALIAS<n> entries are posted individually, one statement per request. Relations found existing in step 6 are skipped; for those that only lack qualifiers, the missing qualifiers are added to the existing statement (a PATCH of its qualifiers) instead of writing it again.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The upload layer handles MaRDI Portal communication errors gracefully:

Condition Behaviour Timeout / connection error Retry with exponential back-off (5 attempts in total) HTTP 429 (rate limit) Wait for the Retry-After duration (seconds or HTTP date, at most 60 seconds), then retry HTTP 403 / 5xx Retry with exponential back-off (5 attempts in total); the portal sometimes answers 403 when it is merely unstable HTTP 422 item-label-description-duplicate Link the conflicting existing item instead of creating a new one and continue; the result page notes that the item's details from the questionnaire were not added to it Any other HTTP 422 Stop the upload with a plain-language reason (e.g. label and description are identical) Any other HTTP error Stop the upload with the item or relation concerned and the portal's message

If the upload stops after something has already been created, everything created so far is still written back to the RDMO project (step 10) and the result page is shown with an Upload incomplete banner. Exporting again continues from there instead of creating the same items twice.

docs.title: 10. Success Page and Catalog Update
docs.text:
After all items and relations have been posted, compare_items() compares the initial payload (before upload) with the final payload (after upload, containing real QIDs) to identify every newly created item. replace_ids() then updates all matching RDMO project Values in place:

  • Wikidata items: the external_id is updated from wikidata:<QID> to mardi:<QID> and [wikidata] is replaced by [mardi] in the text field.
  • User-defined items: Values referencing not found are matched by their label/description pair and updated to mardi:<QID>. ID-question Values (where text is "not found") are resolved via sibling Name/Description Values at the same set index.
  • Publications created from a DOI: their ID question gets the new item, as for the other user-defined items.

After the catalog update, a success page is rendered showing the exported data in two switchable views. Items that were linked to an existing duplicate instead of being created are listed in a Please note box above the views.

docs.title: List View
docs.text:
All newly created MaRDI Portal items are shown grouped by class (Mathematical Model, Research Problem, Formula, …, Publication, Author, Journal) in a fixed display order. Each item is rendered as a collapsible section showing every statement that was written to the portal as property → value lines.

  • Portal item objects are shown as clickable blue links to the item's portal page.
  • External identifiers and URLs (Wikidata QID, DOI, ORCID, swMath work ID, MORwiki ID, zbMATH author ID, ISSN, QUDT quantity kind / constant, and plain URLs) are resolved to their canonical base URLs and rendered as clickable links. User-entered URLs only become links if they use http or https; other schemes (e.g. git://) are shown as text.
  • Quantity values are displayed as the numeric amount followed by the unit name. If the unit is a named portal item it is rendered as a clickable blue link. The dimensionless unit 1 is suppressed.
  • Formulas stored with the math datatype are typeset inline using MathJax (Apache 2.0).
  • Qualifier statements are shown indented below their parent statement.
  • Relations to existing items are shown in a separate section at the bottom. A statement that was on the portal already and only got qualifiers is marked (existing statement, qualifiers added:) and lists only the added qualifiers.

docs.title: Graph View
docs.text:
An interactive network diagram built with Cytoscape.js (MIT) provides a visual overview of the exported data.

Node types:

Shape Colour Meaning Circle Distinct colour per class Newly created MaRDI Portal item Circle Grey Existing MaRDI Portal item (referenced but not created) Rectangle Light yellow Literal value (text, number, URL, …)

Formulas replace their node label with a rendered MathJax image inside the node rectangle.

Clicking any circle node opens its MaRDI Portal page in a new tab. Clicking any rectangle node that has an associated URL opens the external URL.

Edges are directed and labelled with the property name. Quantity nodes are connected to their unit via an additional unit edge.

Qualifier tooltip: clicking an edge opens a floating tooltip listing all qualifier statements for that edge.

Zoom and pan: standard Cytoscape scroll-to-zoom and drag-to-pan apply. The fit button resets the viewport to show all nodes.

docs.title: Filter Panel
docs.text:
A collapsible Filter panel on the graph view lets users reduce visual noise:

  • Legend (class toggles): clicking a class label dims it and hides all nodes of that class together with their edges.
  • Node-type toggles: separate Hide literal nodes and Hide existing items checkboxes toggle those entire node layers.
  • Property checklist: each distinct edge-label has a checkbox; unchecking a property hides all edges with that label. Literal nodes that become fully disconnected are automatically hidden.

All filter dimensions compose: the effective visibility of any node or edge is the intersection of all active filters.

docs.title: Handlers
docs.text: When a user selects an existing item from the MaRDI Portal or Wikidata in a questionnaire field, MaRDMO automatically retrieves and fills in all associated metadata — labels, descriptions, relations, and linked sub-entities — without any manual copying. This is the job of the handlers.

docs.title: Signal Wiring
docs.text:
RDMO emits a value_created or value_updated signal every time a questionnaire answer is saved by the user. MaRDMO registers signal receivers in router.py.

At startup, build_handler_map() constructs a nested lookup table:

{ catalog_uri: { attribute_uri: handler_method } }

On each incoming signal the router checks the active catalog and the URI of the saved attribute, and dispatches to the matching handler method. A separate DELETE_HANDLER_MAP handles cleanup when a value is removed: it deletes all dependent answers that were previously filled in for that entity.

docs.title: Why Not Django Signals for the Cascade?
docs.text:
value_editor() — the helper that writes answers back into the project — saves values directly to the database. If these writes triggered Django signals, every programmatic fill would re-activate handlers, creating runaway cascades.

More critically, during an RDMO project import all values are written to the database in bulk while Django signals are already active. Using signals for the fill cascade would cause handlers to fire out of order against a partially-loaded project, producing incomplete or corrupt results. MaRDMO therefore uses direct function calls for all handler-to-handler cascading, ensuring that fills only happen in response to genuine user interactions.

docs.title: Handler Flow
docs.text:
The sequence when a user picks a Mathematical Model from the portal:

  1. RDMO emits value_created / value_updated for the model ID field.
  2. The router dispatches to Information.model(instance).
  3. model() calls _entry(), which collects the selected QID and calls _fill_model_batch().
  4. _fetch_by_source() fires a SPARQL query (against MaRDI Portal, and optionally Wikidata) to retrieve the model's metadata; for the large MaRDI queries it runs the query in parts (see Split Queries).
  5. _fill_model_batch() writes labels, descriptions, aliases, properties, and relations into the appropriate questionnaire pages via value_editor().
  6. For each related sub-entity type (Research Problems, Mathematical Formulations, Computational Tasks, …), _fill_model_batch() calls _hydrate_relatants(), which in turn calls the corresponding _fill_*_batch() method directly — no signal is emitted.
  7. Each _fill_*_batch() call batches its SPARQL query across all entities of that type at once. For example, if the selected model contains ten Mathematical Formulations, all ten are fetched in a single query and then distributed across the ten questionnaire pages. The same applies to linked Research Problems, Computational Tasks, and so on. Linked publications are fetched the same way, with one query per source (MaRDI Portal, Wikidata) for up to 50 publications.
  8. A visited set is passed through the entire call tree to prevent infinite loops when entities reference each other cyclically.

The batching principle ensures that the number of SPARQL queries scales with the number of distinct entity types in the cascade, not with the number of individual entities.

docs.title: Split Queries
docs.text:
The MaRDI Portal answers queries with many OPTIONAL blocks slowly: the cost grows faster than the number of blocks, and blocks with several values each (aliases, relations, publications) multiply each other's rows before they are grouped. The MaRDI queries for models, formulations, tasks and quantities (and their basics variants) therefore exist only as parts, in model/queries/split/ (task_mardi_1.sparql, task_mardi_2.sparql, …), each with about four blocks. The handlers still name the query by its path (model/queries/task_mardi.sparql), and _fetch_by_source() runs its parts instead; every other query, including all Wikidata queries, is a single file as before.

query_sparql_parts() runs the parts one after another and merges their rows:

  • the first part contains the required patterns and decides which items exist and how many rows each has; if it finds nothing, the other parts are not run;
  • every further part returns one row per item with its own columns, which are added to that item's rows;
  • if any part fails, no item of the batch is filled.

The merged rows have the shape of a single query's rows, so the parsing in model/models.py does not depend on the split. Which part requests which column, and the rules for changing the parts, are listed in the README of the split queries.

docs.title: Database Writes and Network Requests
docs.text:
Selecting a large item writes hundreds of values. The router therefore runs every handler inside helpers.batched_writes():

  • On PostgreSQL and MySQL, the writes of value_editor() are collected in one transaction, which is committed before every request to an external service and at the end. The database is never locked while MaRDMO waits for the network. If a handler fails, only the writes since the last commit are rolled back.
  • On SQLite, every value is still committed on its own. SQLite locks the whole database, and a longer transaction that reads before it writes fails with database is locked when another user saves at the same time.
  • Attributes looked up by URI are remembered until the handler finishes.

All requests to external services go through queries.http_session(), which commits the pending writes and reuses one HTTP session per thread, so repeated requests to the same service keep their connection open.

A handler runs inside the request that saves the answer, so a struggling portal must not hold it for minutes:

  • A SPARQL query is given up after 30 seconds and retried once on a timeout, a connection error, or the answers 429, 502, 503 and 504, after the portal's Retry-After (at most 10 seconds) or 2 seconds. If it fails again, the items of that query are not filled and the failure is logged.
  • wbgetentities retries with backoff, caps every wait (including Retry-After) at 20 seconds and stops retrying after 45 seconds per batch.
  • The same rule (queries.request_with_retry()) retries the portal's TeX check once; the checks before an export retry twice (see Export).

The portal returns the values of a list column (relations, aliases, publications, …) in no fixed order. helpers.split_value() sorts them, relatants thereby by ID, so adding the same item twice fills the same pages in the same order.

docs.title: Pre-Save Validation
docs.text:
In addition to the post-save handler dispatch, MaRDMO registers a pre_save receiver on the RDMO Value model. Before an answer is written to the database, the router looks up the attribute URI in PRESAVE_VALIDATOR_MAP (assembled by build_presave_validator_map() in builders.py) and calls the matching validator. A validator raises rest_framework.exceptions.ValidationError to reject the value; RDMO then shows the message below the question in the interview.

Only answers saved through the interview are validated. Writes made by the handlers themselves run inside helpers.internal_write() and skip these validators, so importing an item never fails because of a pre-save rule; imported data is checked before the export instead. The rules, the places where they are applied, and the exceptions are described in Validation.

docs.title: Dynamic Optionset Providers
docs.text: Many questionnaire fields in MaRDMO require the user to reference an external entity — a piece of software, a mathematical model, an algorithm, a research problem, and so on. These fields are backed by dynamic optionset providers: Python classes that the RDMO frontend calls whenever the user types into an autocomplete widget, returning a ranked list of matching items from external knowledge bases or from the current project.

docs.title: One Provider, One Table
docs.text:
Every option set of the questionnaire names its provider by a key (provider_key), and RDMO creates the provider from the setting OPTIONSET_PROVIDERS as Class(key, label, class_name). It asks the provider for options with the search text only — not with the question — so a provider cannot tell which question it serves; it knows its key. MaRDMO therefore has one provider class, MaRDMO.providers.MaRDMOProvider, and a table in MaRDMO.optionsets with one row per key:

'RelatedQuantityWithoutCreation': Search('Options for related Quantities without Creation',
                                         'quantity', answers=['quantity'], sources=['mardi']),

A row names the item class (or classes) of the MaRDI Portal search, the questionnaire sections whose items of the user's own are offered too, whether a new item may be created, the sources, whether "not found" is offered, whether RDMO reloads the page after a selection (refresh), and from how many characters the search starts. A new option set needs one row.

MaRDMO.optionsets.OPTIONSET_PROVIDERS is the setting for all rows, so an RDMO installation adds it with one line (see the installation instructions). Up to MaRDMO 0.6 every key had a class of its own (MaRDMO.model.providers.MathematicalModel and so on); settings that still list these must be replaced by that line. Providers of programming languages and software search from the first character, since some of their names have only one (C, R); all others start at three, since a single letter matches hundreds of items and slows the search.

docs.title: Three Provider Tiers
docs.text: Providers are organised into three tiers of increasing capability.

docs.title: Tier 1 — Pure search
docs.text: The simplest providers query the MaRDI Portal, or the MaRDI Portal and Wikidata, and return whatever matches. A "not found" option is sometimes included so the user can explicitly signal that no appropriate item exists.

docs.title: Tier 2 — Search + project items
docs.text: Tier 2 providers extend Tier 1 by also surfacing items the user has already defined or selected elsewhere in the current RDMO project. This lets a user re-reference an entity they documented in an earlier section without having to look it up again.

docs.title: Tier 3 — Search + project items + inline creation
docs.text: The most capable providers add the ability to create a new item on the fly. The user types a plain-text label and a short description — the same two pieces of information that a result returned from an external source would carry — and the provider wraps this in a special option that later triggers item creation in the MaRDI Portal during export. Items entered this way are visually distinguishable from portal or Wikidata results by the absence of a source tag: a portal result appears as Euler method (numerical ODE solver) [mardi], a Wikidata result as Euler method (numerical ODE solver) [wikidata], while an inline-created item appears as My solver (custom ODE solver) with no tag.

docs.title: MaRDI Portal vs Wikidata Search
docs.text: For the MaRDI Portal, providers use a class-restricted search: only items that are an instance of the relevant item class are returned. For Wikidata, an unrestricted search is used instead — equivalent to typing a term directly into the Wikidata search bar. The reason for this asymmetry is that Wikidata's class hierarchy is too heterogeneous for reliable filtering: a piece of software might be instance of free software rather than instance of software, making a class-restricted query miss many valid results.

docs.title: Autocomplete Mechanism
docs.text:
The following steps happen each time the user types in an autocomplete field:

  1. Debounced request — after a short pause the browser sends an HTTP request to the Django backend, passing the current search term.

  2. query_api_per_class — the backend fires a CirrusSearch query against the MediaWiki API. CirrusSearch is the Elasticsearch-backed full-text search engine embedded in Wikibase/MediaWiki. The haswbstatement keyword is a CirrusSearch extension that filters results to items carrying a specific property-value pair:

    GET /w/api.php ?action=query &list=search &srsearch=euler* haswbstatement:P31=Q68663 &format=json

    Here P31 is the instance of property and Q68663 is the item class QID (e.g. mathematical model). The trailing * enables prefix matching so partial input is handled gracefully.

  3. wbgetentities follow-up — the QIDs returned by the search are resolved to English labels and descriptions via a second API call:

    GET /w/api.php ?action=wbgetentities &ids=Q42|Q137|Q951 &props=labels|descriptions &languages=en &format=json

  4. Cache — the results of each source (MaRDI Portal, Wikidata) are kept in Django's cache for five minutes, keyed by search text and item class. Repeated searches — while typing, or for the same entity type on another page — are then answered without querying the portal again. Failed requests are not cached, so the next search tries again. The results do not depend on the project, so the user's own answers cannot make them outdated.

  5. Duplicates — a Wikidata result with the same label (ignoring case) and the same description as a MaRDI Portal result is left out: it is the same item, and the export would ask the user to select the MaRDI Portal one. Results without a description are never merged, since a label alone does not make two items the same.

  6. Merge and return — for Tier 2 and 3 providers, the matching items the user has already entered in the project are put before the external results, and the list is returned to the autocomplete widget. These project items are read from the database on every request (two queries, regardless of how many entity types the provider covers), so an item saved a moment ago is offered right away.

docs.title: Publication Retrieval
docs.text: Publication fields in MaRDMO can be filled in two ways: the user can select an existing item directly from the MaRDI Portal or Wikidata, or they can enter a DOI and let MaRDMO fetch the metadata automatically. This page describes the DOI lookup path and how authors and journals are resolved.

docs.title: Source Cascade
docs.text:
When a DOI is entered MaRDMO queries multiple sources in two stages.

Stage 1 — Knowledge graphs (parallel): The MaRDI Portal and Wikidata are queried simultaneously via SPARQL. If either source returns a result, Stage 2 is skipped entirely and the found metadata is used.

Stage 2 — External APIs (parallel, only if Stage 1 yields nothing): CrossRef, DataCite, zbMath, and the DOI metadata service are queried simultaneously:

Source Endpoint CrossRef https://api.crossref.org/works/{doi} DataCite https://api.datacite.org/dois/{doi} zbMath https://api.zbmath.org/v1/document/_structured_search?DOI={doi} DOI metadata https://citation.doi.org/metadata?doi={doi}

The first source in that order that returns a valid response with a title wins.

Once the primary metadata has been retrieved, the ORCiD public API is queried to find researchers associated with the DOI:

https://pub.orcid.org/v3.0/expanded-search/?q=doi-self:"{doi}"

The expanded search returns the names together with the ORCiD iDs, so one request suffices however many researchers list the DOI.

The results enrich author records with ORCiD identifiers regardless of which primary source was chosen.

docs.title: Author Resolution
docs.text:
After the primary publication metadata has been retrieved, MaRDMO attempts to resolve each author to a persistent identifier:

  1. Each author may carry an ORCiD (from CrossRef, DataCite, DOI API, or the ORCiD enrichment step) and/or a zbMath author code (from zbMath).
  2. These identifiers are used to search Wikidata for the author's QID.
  3. The ORCiD, zbMath code, and Wikidata QID together are then used to search the MaRDI Portal for the author's portal QID.
  4. If the author matches no MaRDI Portal or Wikidata item but has an ORCiD or zbMath code, the export creates a new author item with these identifiers (instance of human, MaRDI person profile).
  5. An author without any identifier is stored as a plain name string attached to the publication record.

Authors are matched by identifiers only, never by name: two authors with the same name are different people unless they share an identifier. The rules are:

  • Order of identifiers: if the identifiers of an author point to different items, the ORCiD decides, then the zbMath code, then the Wikidata QID.
  • MaRDI Portal first: per author, an item on the MaRDI Portal is preferred over one on Wikidata. An item found on Wikidata adds its QID to the author's identifiers, so the MaRDI Portal item holding that Wikidata QID matches as well.
  • "None" is no identifier: some MaRDI Portal items carry the text None as zbMath code; it does not match anything.
  • One item, one author: an item is given to one author only. Wikidata often lists an author both as item and as name string; the name string then stays a name string, so the export cites the authors as Wikidata does.

docs.title: Journal Resolution
docs.text:
1. The ISSN is extracted from whichever primary source provided the publication metadata.
  2. The ISSN is used to search Wikidata for the journal's QID.
  3. The ISSN and the Wikidata QID together are used to search the MaRDI Portal for the journal's portal QID.
  4. If a match is found anywhere the existing item is reused; if not, a new journal item is created during export with the ISSN as an identifier, as instance of scientific journal with the MaRDI journal profile.

As for authors, journals are matched by identifiers only: the ISSN decides before the Wikidata QID, the MaRDI Portal comes before Wikidata, and a MaRDI Portal journal also matches through its Wikidata QID.

docs.title: Field Mapping
docs.text:
The table below shows which field each source provides and how it maps to the MaRDMO publication record.

Field MaRDI Portal / Wikidata (SPARQL) CrossRef DataCite zbMath DOI API Title label title[0] titles[0].title title.title title Description arbitrary string generated by MaRDMO ← ← ← ← Entry type entrytypelabel type types.bibtex document_type.description type Date date published.date-parts dates (Issued) year published.date-parts Volume volume volume relatedItems[0].volume source.series[0].volume volume Issue issue issue relatedItems[0].issue source.series[0].issue issue Page page page firstPage–lastPage source.page page DOI doi DOI doi links[doi].identifier DOI Language languagelabel language language language.languages language Authors authorInfos (SPARQL) author[].given + family + ORCiD creators[].givenName + familyName + nameIdentifiers[ORCID] contributors.authors[].name + codes[0] author[].given + family + ORCiD Journal journalInfo (SPARQL) ISSN + container-title relatedIdentifiers + relatedItems source.series ISSN + container-title

Titles and names fetched from these sources are cleaned when they are stored, since users cannot edit this background data: line breaks become spaces, formatting tags such as <i> or <sup> are removed, and HTML entities such as & are decoded. Preprints (Crossref posted-content, CSL article) count as scholarly articles, as on the MaRDI Portal and Wikidata.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Everything MaRDMO exports must be accepted by the MaRDI Portal; a value the portal rejects would otherwise stop the upload halfway. MaRDMO therefore checks entered values in four places, which all use the same rules:

Place When What happens on a problem Pre-save validation While the user types in the interview The answer is not saved; the message appears below the question Preview First click on Export to MaRDI Portal The value is shown with a red marker explaining the problem Documentation checks Second click, before anything is posted The export stops with a list of errors Final export check After the payload is built, before anything is posted The export stops with a list of errors

The rules live in one place — validators.py, with the regular expressions in patterns.py — so that the four places always agree. The preview uses them through template filters in templatetags/mardmo_tags.py.

docs.title: Typing rules and complete rules
docs.text: RDMO saves an answer while the user is still typing. Pre-save validation can therefore only reject what can never become valid by typing on: 1, 10. and 10.1000/ are all accepted for a DOI, because each can still become a complete DOI. These typing rules are kept separately from the complete rules that the preview, the checks and the export apply, e.g. DOI_RE (typing) and DOI_STRICT_RE (complete) in patterns.py. Where every prefix of a valid value is itself valid (a swMATH ID consists of digits only), one rule serves all four places.

docs.title: Rules by field
docs.text:
Field While typing Before the export Short descriptions At most 2000 characters Additionally: present, and not identical to the name Long descriptions and other answers exported as text No line breaks No line breaks Relations (Label (Description)) Format Label (Description) or Label (Description) [source] — Data properties No mutually exclusive pair (e.g. linear and nonlinear) Same QUDT IDs Starts with an uppercase letter, then letters, _ or - At least two characters DOIs (publications, references, documentation, data set publication) A beginning of 10.NNNN/suffix; links (https://doi.org/…) are rejected Complete 10.NNNN/suffix (sub-prefixes such as 10.1000.10/ allowed) URLs (references, documentation) No spaces or forbidden characters, a beginning of an allowed scheme, at most 500 characters Additionally: an allowed scheme and a domain such as example.org swMATH IDs Digits only; links are rejected Same Archival year Up to four digits Exactly four digits Counts (compute nodes, CPU occurrence, processor cores, data size in items) Digits without a leading zero Whole number of at least 1 Data size (kilobyte to terabyte) Digits with at most one dot; a decimal comma is rejected with a hint Positive decimal with a dot (12, 1.5) Formulas and formula symbols — Accepted by the MaRDI Portal's TeX checker (see below); no % comment in multi-line formulas Symbol table of a formula or quantity definition — Every symbol has a quantity; a symbol stands for exactly one quantity, and no symbol appears twice with the same quantity (see below)

The symbol table belongs to the formula or quantity, not to one formula field: whether the formula fields hold an equation system (e.g. in an align environment) or several equivalent formulas, a symbol stands for the same quantity in all of them. Several symbols may stand for one quantity (k_1, k_2 for a reaction rate constant); different formulas may use the same symbol for different quantities. Symbols are compared as they are exported (line breaks and outer whitespace removed). A symbol fetched from the MaRDI Portal without symbol represents comes into the questionnaire without a quantity, so the checks and the preview ask for it.

Allowed URL schemes are http and https; the source code repository URL additionally accepts git, ssh, svn, cvs, bzr and ftp. Only http and https URLs are turned into links on the export result page.

docs.title: Final export check
docs.text:
GeneratePayload.validate_identifiers() runs on the finished payload, before the relation existence check and before anything is posted. It checks every statement and qualifier of the following kinds and lists all problems at once:

  • URL values (url datatype)
  • DOI and swMATH work ID values
  • time values (+YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ)
  • quantity amounts (+8, +1.5)

It also checks that every Item<n> placeholder in the payload belongs to an item of the export: a placeholder is replaced by the item's QID while posting, so one without an item would be rejected by the MaRDI Portal after other items were created already.

This catches values that reached the payload without passing the other checks, for example data written before a rule existed.

docs.title: Normalisation on export
docs.text:
Some differences are fixed on export instead of being reported, because they never change the meaning of a value but would make the portal reject it:

Values Normalisation Text, external IDs, URLs Tabs become spaces; leading and trailing whitespace is removed Formulas and formula symbols Line breaks and tabs become spaces; leading and trailing whitespace is removed Quantity amounts Whitespace and leading zeros are removed (08 → +8) Archival year, reference and documentation texts Leading and trailing whitespace is removed

TeX reads a line break as a space, so a formula written over several lines keeps its meaning; \\ line breaks inside environments such as cases are unchanged. The one exception is a % comment, which runs to the end of its line: joining the lines would hide the rest of the formula. Multi-line formulas containing a % comment are therefore reported (\%, a percent sign, is fine).

docs.title: Formula check
docs.text:
The portal validates formulas with its own TeX checker (texvc), which accepts less than LaTeX, KaTeX or MathJax. MaRDMO sends every formula and formula symbol to that checker (tex_check.py) when the preview is rendered and when the documentation checks run:

  • Formulas are checked in parallel, with a timeout of 5 seconds, in the form in which they are exported (on one line).
  • Verdicts are cached for a week, so unchanged formulas are not sent again. Failed requests are not cached.
  • If the checker cannot be reached, the preview marks the formula as not verified by the MaRDI Portal and the checks do not report it; the portal still checks it during the upload.

In the preview, a rejected formula is not handed to MathJax (an unbalanced brace would otherwise swallow the rest of the line). It is shown as raw TeX with a marker; the browser adds MathJax's explanation, e.g. Missing close brace (partials/_mathjax_errors.html). Formulas that MathJax itself cannot render are shown the same way instead of MathJax's error box.

Environments. The checker only answers syntax error, also for environments it does not support, although KaTeX and MathJax render them. When a rejected formula contains such an environment, MaRDMO names it and lists the supported ones. Accepted by the MaRDI Portal (tested October 2026):

aligned, alignedat, align, cases, array, matrix, pmatrix, bmatrix, Bmatrix, vmatrix, Vmatrix, smallmatrix

Starred variants (align*, cases*, …) are never accepted, nor are, for example, equation, gather, gathered, split, multline and eqnarray. The list is kept in tex_check.SUPPORTED_ENVIRONMENTS.

docs.title: Which writes are checked
docs.text:
Pre-save validation guards what the user types in the interview: it only runs for answers saved through RDMO's project value API, which the interview uses (the router remembers the path of the current request and checks it). Everything else saves values without pre-save validation and is checked by the preview, the checks and the export like all other data:

  • Project imports — an RDMO project file may contain values written before a rule existed; rejecting them would make the import fail halfway.
  • MaRDMO's own writes — values written by the handlers when an item is imported from the MaRDI Portal or Wikidata, and the IDs written back after an export. These run inside helpers.internal_write(), which also covers handler writes during an interview request.
  • Snapshots — creating a snapshot copies values, rolling back restores them; both were valid when they were saved.
  • Management commands, scripts and fixture loads, which run outside a request.

In addition, adders.py drops imported values that cannot be stored consistently: of a mutually exclusive pair of data properties, both are dropped (neither side can be judged correct), and QUDT IDs that do not match the complete format are skipped. The documentation checks report what is missing, so the user can complete it.

To add a rule for a new field, see How to Validate a New Field.

docs.title: How to Add a Data Property
docs.text:
A data property is a boolean characteristic of a MathModDB entity — for example is dimensional or is physical constant. When a user selects such a property in the RDMO interview, MaRDMO validates the selection, writes it to the questionnaire, checks it before export, and maps it to a Wikibase statement on the MaRDI Portal.

Properties come in two flavours:

  • Class-dependent — the corresponding MaRDI Portal item has a different name per entity class. Example: is dimensional maps to "dimensional model", "dimensional formula", "dimensional quantity", "dimensional quantity kind" — separate Wikibase items for each class.
  • Class-independent — one Wikibase item is used regardless of entity class. Example: is physical constant maps to "physical constant" for every entity class that supports it.

The two walkthroughs below use these properties as concrete examples. Both properties are part of the MaRDMO Catalogs for detailed and basic documentation of mathematical models.

!!! note "Quantity and Quantity Kind" The entity classes Quantity and Quantity Kind are treated together in the backend under the key quantity. They share one MaRDI Portal query (the parts split/quantity_mardi_*.sparql) and one Wikidata query (quantity_wikidata.sparql), where both item types are covered via a UNION pattern.

docs.title: Step 1a — Add the Option to RDMO
docs.text:
Create a new option with the URI https://rdmo.mardi4nfdi.de/terms/options/mathmoddb/is-dimensional and add it to each relevant optionset in RDMO. For is dimensional the relevant optionsets are:

  • https://rdmo.mardi4nfdi.de/terms/options/model-properties
  • https://rdmo.mardi4nfdi.de/terms/options/formulation-properties
  • https://rdmo.mardi4nfdi.de/terms/options/quantity-properties

See How to Create a New Option and How to Create a New Optionset for further information.

docs.title: Step 1b — Register the Option in model/data/mapping.json
docs.text:
Add an entry to model/data/mapping.json. This file maps MathModDB property keys to their RDMO option URIs and human-readable labels:

{"key": "is_dimensional", "url": "https://rdmo.mardi4nfdi.de/terms/options/mathmoddb/is-dimensional", "label": "is dimensional"}

docs.title: Step 2 — Register MaRDI Portal QIDs
docs.text:
Add one entry per entity class to data/items.json (productive portal) and data/items_staging.json (staging portal, for testing purposes):

data/items.json:

"dimensional model":         "Q6775551",
"dimensional formula":       "Q6775550",
"dimensional quantity":      "Q6775552",
"dimensional quantity kind": "Q6775553"

data/items_staging.json:

"dimensional model":         "Q13324",
"dimensional formula":       "Q13323",
"dimensional quantity":      "Q13325",
"dimensional quantity kind": "Q13326"

docs.title: Step 3 — model/constants.py
docs.text:
3a — Mutual exclusion pair (is dimensional and is dimensionless cannot both be true at the same time):

data_properties_check = [
    ...
    ('is_dimensionless', 'is_dimensional'),
]

3b — Entity classes that carry this property (model, formula, quantity, quantity kind):

data_properties_per_class = {
    'model':       [..., 'is_dimensional'],
    'formulation': [..., 'is_dimensional'],
    'quantity':    [..., 'is_dimensional'],
}

3c — Register as class-dependent. The second element is the item name prefix; MaRDMO appends the entity class name automatically to look up the correct Wikibase item ("dimensional model", "dimensional formula", etc.):

DEPENDENT_PROPERTIES = [
    ...
    ('is_dimensional', 'dimensional'),
]

docs.title: Step 4 — SPARQL Queries
docs.text:
For each entity class the property applies to, edit the corresponding queries in model/queries/ — both the MaRDI and Wikidata variants, and both the full and -basics variants where they exist. The MaRDI queries of these classes exist only as parts in model/queries/split/; its README.md lists which part requests which column.

Affected files for is dimensional:

Entity class Files Model split/model_mardi_*.sparql, model_wikidata.sparql, split/model-basics_mardi_*.sparql, model-basics_wikidata.sparql Formula split/formulation_mardi_*.sparql, formulation_wikidata.sparql, split/formulation-basics_mardi_*.sparql, formulation-basics_wikidata.sparql Quantity + Quantity Kind split/quantity_mardi_*.sparql, quantity_wikidata.sparql

MaRDI Portal queries (split/*_mardi_*.sparql): in each split query, pick one part other than part 1 with fewer than four OPTIONAL blocks (or start a new part with the next number) and add ?is_dimensional to its SELECT and GROUP BY clauses, then update the table in split/README.md. For model and formula queries, add a single OPTIONAL block with a trailing BIND:

OPTIONAL {{ ?id wdt:{instance of} wd:{dimensional model}. BIND("True" AS ?is_dimensional_raw) }}
    BIND(COALESCE(?is_dimensional_raw, "False") AS ?is_dimensional)

Use {dimensional formula} in the formula files. For the quantity file, both item types are combined via UNION since only one file covers both:

OPTIONAL {{ {{ ?id wdt:{instance of} wd:{dimensional quantity}. }} UNION {{ ?id wdt:{instance of} wd:{dimensional quantity kind}. }} BIND("True" AS ?is_dimensional_raw) }}
    BIND(COALESCE(?is_dimensional_raw, "False") AS ?is_dimensional)

Wikidata queries (*_wikidata.sparql): the items "dimensional model", "dimensional formula", "dimensional quantity", and "dimensional quantity kind" do not currently exist in Wikidata, so there is nothing to add to the Wikidata SPARQL queries. Should these items be created in Wikidata in the future, the corresponding blocks can be added at that point using the actual Wikidata QIDs.

docs.title: Step 1a — Add the Option to RDMO
docs.text:
Create a new option with the URI https://rdmo.mardi4nfdi.de/terms/options/mathmoddb/is-physical-constant and add it to the relevant optionset. For is physical constant the relevant optionset is:

  • https://rdmo.mardi4nfdi.de/terms/options/quantity-properties

See How to Create a New Option and How to Create a New Optionset for further information.

docs.title: Step 1b — Register the Option in model/data/mapping.json
docs.text: {"key": "is_physical_constant", "url": "https://rdmo.mardi4nfdi.de/terms/options/mathmoddb/is-physical-constant", "label": "is physical constant"}

docs.title: Step 2 — Register MaRDI Portal QIDs
docs.text:
A single item is shared across all entity classes:

data/items.json:

"physical constant": "Q6534290"

data/items_staging.json:

"physical constant": "Q1777"

docs.title: Step 3 — model/constants.py
docs.text:
3a — Mutual exclusion pairs (is physical constant is mutually exclusive with both is mathematical constant and is chemical constant):

data_properties_check = [
    ...
    ('is_mathematical_constant', 'is_physical_constant'),
    ('is_physical_constant',     'is_chemical_constant'),
]

3b — Entity classes (is physical constant applies to quantities and quantity kinds only):

data_properties_per_class = {
    'quantity': [..., 'is_physical_constant'],
}

3c — Register as class-independent. The second element is the full item name used for all entity classes:

INDEPENDENT_PROPERTIES = [
    ...
    ('is_physical_constant', 'physical constant'),
]

docs.title: Step 4 — SPARQL Queries
docs.text:
Only the quantity queries need updating: one part of split/quantity_mardi_*.sparql (as in Case 1) and quantity_wikidata.sparql.

Add ?is_physical_constant to SELECT and GROUP BY of that part and of the Wikidata query, then add the OPTIONAL block in the WHERE clause.

MaRDI Portal:

OPTIONAL {{ ?id wdt:{instance of} wd:{physical constant}. BIND("True" AS ?is_physical_constant_raw) }}
    BIND(COALESCE(?is_physical_constant_raw, "False") AS ?is_physical_constant)

Wikidata: "physical constant" exists in Wikidata as Q173227, so the corresponding block should be added to the Wikidata query:

OPTIONAL {{ ?id wdt:P31 wd:Q173227. BIND("True" AS ?is_physical_constant_raw) }}
    BIND(COALESCE(?is_physical_constant_raw, "False") AS ?is_physical_constant)

docs.title: Adding Export Support for a New Entity
docs.text:
When a new entity type is added to a MaRDMO submodule, four stages of the pipeline need to be extended: pre-processing, HTML preview, validation, and portal export. This page describes each stage and the helpers available for implementing it.

For the full end-to-end export flow from the user's perspective, see Export Pipeline.

docs.title: 1. Pre-processing (optional)
docs.text:
File: <submodule>/worker.py — class Prepare*, method preview

Before the answers dict is passed to the template, an optional pre-processing step can augment it with display-ready structures. This is only needed when nested or paired data must be flattened or grouped for the template to iterate over directly, for example:

wf_data['model_task_pairs'] = [...]         # Workflow: models + their tasks
ps_data['algorithm_software_pairs'] = [...]  # Process step: algorithms + software/hardware/docs
ps_data['method_instrument_pairs']  = [...]  # Process step: methods + instruments/docs
hw_data['cpu_entries']              = [...]  # Hardware: CPUs with counts and cores

If the new entity's data can be rendered directly from the answers dict without restructuring, this step can be skipped.

docs.title: 2. HTML Preview
docs.text:
File: templates/MaRDMO/<catalog>Template.html (e.g. modelTemplate.html, workflowTemplate.html), with shared blocks in templates/MaRDMO/partials/

The answers dict (augmented by pre-processing if applicable) is passed to a Django template as context. Add a new section to the relevant template to render the new entity's fields.

!!! note Errors (missing required fields, invalid values) are flagged with red text at this stage so the user can correct them before committing to the export. Value formats are checked with the template filters in templatetags/mardmo_tags.py (e.g. url_problem, doi_problem, count_problem), which use the same rules as the checks and the export; see Validation.

docs.title: 3. Validation
docs.text:
File: checks/model.py, checks/algorithm.py, or checks/workflow.py

The Checks class (checks/__init__.py) composes three mixins, each exposing one entry-point method:

Method Catalog scope Checks.run_model(project, data, catalog) Model catalog Checks.run_algorithm(project, data, catalog) Algorithm catalog Checks.run_workflow(project, data, catalog) Workflow catalog

These methods validate the collected answers for completeness and consistency and return an error list that aborts the export if non-empty. Add checks for any mandatory fields or cross-entity constraints introduced by the new entity. For the format of individual values, reuse the shared rules in validators.py — see How to Validate a New Field.

docs.title: 4. Portal Export
docs.text:
File: <submodule>/worker.py — class Prepare*, method export

The export method translates the answers dict into Wikibase statements. The following helpers are available on the payload object:

docs.title: Statement helpers
docs.text:
add_answer(verb, object_and_type, qualifier=None, subject=None) Add a single statement. Automatically routes to a batch statement (new item) or a RELATION entry (existing item).

payload.add_answer(
    verb            = self.properties["instance of"],
    object_and_type = [item_key, "wikibase-item"],
    qualifier       = qualifiers,
)

add_answers(mardmo_property, wikibase_property, datatype="string") Iterate over all values stored under mardmo_property in the current subject and call add_answer for each.

payload.add_answers("descriptionLong", "description", datatype="string")

docs.title: Relation helpers
docs.text:
add_single_relation(statement, alt_statement=None, qualifier=None, reverse=False) Add one statement per entry in subject[statement["relatant"]]. Uses the portal item key when the relatant is in the payload dictionary; falls back to alt_statement (string value) otherwise. Set reverse=True to swap subject and object.

add_multiple_relation(statement, optional_qualifier=None, reverse=False) Add one statement per (relation, relatant) pair. Supported optional qualifier type: "assumes". Forward/backward direction and the role (object has role, e.g. for contains initial condition) are read from the mapping data; set reverse=True to override the direction.

docs.title: Specialised helpers
docs.text:
add_data_properties(item_class) Add instance of statements for each data property checkbox selected on the current subject (e.g. dimensional, deterministic).

add_in_defining_formula() Add in defining formula statements with symbol represents qualifiers, used for mathematical formulations and quantities.

add_aliases(aliases_dict) Add alias statements for the current subject item.

docs.title: Qualifier helper
docs.text:
add_qualifier(identifier, data_type, content) Build a qualifier dict to pass to any of the statement helpers above.

qualifiers = payload.add_qualifier(
    self.properties["comment"], "string", comment_text
)

Qualifiers are either meaning or additive qualifiers (see Qualifier Merge): a statement that exists on the MaRDI Portal with the same meaning gets the missing additive qualifiers instead of being written again. A new qualifier is additive unless it is listed in _MEANING_QUALIFIERS in payload.py. A qualifier that makes a statement a different one (like a role or a platform) belongs there, and the property of its statements in _MEANING_PROPERTIES; the static test tests/static/test_meaning_qualifiers.py checks this for roles and platforms.

docs.title: How to Register a Question in MaRDMO
docs.text: MaRDMO reads answers from the RDMO interview by looking up each question's URI and extracting the value according to a set of configuration flags. Registering a new question means adding an entry to the relevant <submodule>/data/questions.json file so that MaRDMO knows where to find the answer and how to store it.

docs.title: Step 1 — Locate the questions.json file
docs.text:
Each submodule has its own registry:

Submodule File Model model/data/questions.json Algorithm algorithm/data/questions.json Workflow workflow/data/questions.json Publication publication/data/questions.json Search search/data/questions.json

Open the file for the submodule the new question belongs to.

docs.title: Step 2 — Add the entry
docs.text:
Add a new key under the appropriate entity group. The minimum required fields are key1, key2, and uri:

"My New Question": {
    "key1": "model",
    "key2": "myfield",
    "uri": "domain/model/myfield"
}

Fill in the remaining fields according to steps 3 and 4 below.

docs.title: Step 3 — Set key1, key2, key3, and uri
docs.text:
key1 is the entity class the answer belongs to (e.g. "model", "quantity", "software"). It becomes the top-level key in the answers dict.

key2 is the specific question name within that entity (e.g. "Name", "Description", "reference"). It becomes the second-level key.

key3 is only needed for deeply nested questions where the same entity block holds multiple sub-fields under one key2 (e.g. "author" → "ID", "Name", "orcid"). Leave it out if not needed.

uri is the RDMO attribute URI fragment — the part after https://rdmo.mardi4nfdi.de/terms/. Check the RDMO admin interface under Domain → Attributes for the exact value.

docs.title: Step 4 — Set the five boolean flags
docs.text: The five flags determine how the answer is extracted and where it is stored. Set only the ones that apply; all others default to false.

docs.title: set_prefix
docs.text: Set to true when the question lives inside a nested question set (a question set that is itself inside a collection page). This inserts the entity instance index into the path so that answers for different instances do not overwrite each other.

docs.title: set_index
docs.text: Set to true when the question lives inside a question set (not a top-level page question). This inserts the question set instance index into the path.

docs.title: collection_index
docs.text: Set to true when the RDMO question is a collection (the user can provide multiple answers for a single question). This appends the answer index to the path.

docs.title: external_id
docs.text: Set to true when the question links to another entity via RDMO's external ID mechanism (e.g. a relatant question that stores a reference to another portal item). The answer is stored as an {ID, Name, Description} dict or as a raw external ID string depending on the path shape — see the Question Configuration Reference.

docs.title: option_text
docs.text: Set to true when the question uses an optionset combined with a free-text field — for example, a reference question where the option identifies the reference type (DOI, URL) and the text holds the actual value. The answer is stored as a [option_uri, text] pair.

docs.title: Step 5 — Look up the correct flag combination
docs.text: Once you have determined which flags apply, consult the Question Configuration Reference to confirm the resulting path and entry type. Make sure the path and type match what the downstream handler code expects for this entity.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
A quantity reference question that lives in a nested question set (set_prefix), is a collection (collection_index), and captures both a reference type option and a URL (option_text):

"Reference": {
    "key1": "quantity",
    "key2": "reference",
    "uri": "domain/quantity/reference",
    "set_prefix": true,
    "collection_index": true,
    "option_text": true
}

This matches flag combo (✓ ✗ ✓ ✗ ✓) → rule 17 → path [quantity, prefix_idx, reference, coll_index] → list entry [option_uri, text].

docs.title: Make a Release
docs.text: A release puts a new MaRDMO version on PyPI and archives it on Zenodo. It starts with pushing a tag; the workflow pypi-publish.yml does the rest and publishes the GitHub release last, so Zenodo (which archives every published release) never archives a version that did not reach PyPI.

docs.title: Before the release
docs.text:
• Manual checks: the scripts of the dev-tests branch (see its README), read-only against the MaRDI Portal.
  • Questionnaire: the MaRDMO-Questionnaire has its own version numbers. If this MaRDMO version needs questionnaire changes, release the questionnaire first and name the MaRDMO version it is meant for in its description. The release workflow tests against the questionnaire's latest release, so a missing questionnaire release stops the MaRDMO release before anything is published. A MaRDMO version without questionnaire changes needs no new questionnaire release.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
1. Version bump: a pull request that changes only __version__ in MaRDMO/__init__.py (pyproject.toml reads it from there); merge it when the tests pass.
  2. Update the local main: git checkout main && git pull, so the tag lands on the merge commit with the new version.
  3. Draft release on GitHub: Draft a new release, tag vX.Y.Z ("create new tag on publish"), title and release notes, then Save draft. A draft creates no tag and Zenodo ignores it.
  4. Push the tag: git tag vX.Y.Z && git push origin vX.Y.Z.

The workflow then runs these jobs, each only if the ones before passed:

Job What it does Tag and version the tag must be v plus the package version Latest questionnaire release finds the questionnaire's latest published release Tests every supported Python and RDMO version, against that questionnaire release, and the documentation Upload to PyPI builds the package and uploads it (Trusted Publishing, environment pypi) Publish the release publishes the draft; without a draft it creates a release with generated notes

Dry run: Actions → Publish to PyPI → Run workflow on any branch runs the first three jobs (without the tag check): nothing is uploaded or published.

docs.title: If something fails
docs.text: What failed What to do Tag and version nothing was published: delete the tag (git push --delete origin vX.Y.Z, git tag -d vX.Y.Z), fix the version with a pull request, push the tag again Tests nothing was published: fix the cause (or release the questionnaire), delete and push the tag again Upload to PyPI nothing was published; if the version is on PyPI already, it cannot be uploaded again: the next version is needed Publish the release the package is on PyPI: run only the failed job again (Re-run failed jobs, or gh run rerun <run> --failed)

docs.title: What runs when
docs.text: Event Tests Documentation Push to any branch one combination (Python 3.14, RDMO 2.5.2) built Pull request to main every combination built Merge into main one combination built and published Release (tag push) every combination, against the questionnaire release built

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• PyPI: a trusted publisher for the project (owner MaRDI4NFDI, repository MaRDMO-Plugin, workflow pypi-publish.yml, environment pypi); renaming the workflow needs the entry to be updated.
  • GitHub environment pypi: deployments only from tags v*.
  • Zenodo: the repository's webhook for releases (Settings → Webhooks).
  • Rulesets: main needs pull requests and the tests; tags v* may only be created, moved or deleted by maintainers.

docs.title: How to Validate a New Field
docs.text:
A value the MaRDI Portal rejects stops the export halfway, so every field with a fixed format is checked in four places: while typing, in the preview, in the documentation checks, and in the final check before anything is posted (see Validation). This page shows how to add such a rule, using the swMATH work ID of a software reference as the example: it must be a number such as 7554, not a link.

All four places call one shared rule, so that they always agree. Write the rule once and only connect it in each place.

docs.title: Step 1 — Decide on the rule
docs.text:
Answer two questions before writing code:

  • What does the portal accept? Check the property on the MaRDI Portal (format constraints, examples). For swMATH work IDs: digits only.
  • Is every beginning of a valid value itself valid? RDMO saves while the user types, so pre-save validation must accept unfinished input.
    • If yes (swMATH: 7, 75, 755 are all valid), one rule serves all four places.
    • If no (a DOI 10. is unfinished, not wrong), write a typing rule that only rejects what can never become valid, and a complete rule for the other three places. Compare DOI_RE and DOI_STRICT_RE in patterns.py.

docs.title: Step 2 — Pattern and shared rule
docs.text:
File: patterns.py — add the regular expression with a docstring that names its format and where it is used:

SWMATH_ID_RE = re.compile(r'^[0-9]+$')
'''swMATH work ID: digits only (format of Wikidata property P6830).

Every prefix of a valid ID is valid, so the same pattern serves the pre-save
validator, the preview, the documentation checker, and the export.
'''

File: validators.py — add a *_problem() function that returns a message for the user, or None if the value is fine. Ignore leading and trailing whitespace (it is removed on export) and treat an empty value as "nothing to check" — whether a value is required is decided elsewhere:

def swmath_problem(swmath_id):
    '''Return what is wrong with a swMATH work ID, or ``None`` if it is valid.'''
    swmath_id = (swmath_id or '').strip()
    if not swmath_id:
        return None
    if _looks_like_link(swmath_id) or '/' in swmath_id:
        return 'Enter only the swMATH number (e.g. 7554), not the link'
    if not SWMATH_ID_RE.match(swmath_id):
        return 'swMATH ID must be a number (e.g. 7554)'
    return None

Messages should say what to enter, ideally with an example, since users see them directly.

docs.title: Step 3 — Pre-save validation
docs.text:
File: validators.py — add a validator that receives the RDMO Value about to be saved and raises rest_framework.exceptions.ValidationError with the message under text. RDMO shows that message below the question. If the question offers several options (DOI, URL, swMATH ID, …), react only to your own option:

def validate_swmath(instance):
    '''Reject a swMATH work ID that is not a number.'''
    if not instance.option or not instance.text:
        return
    if instance.option.uri != get_options().get('SWMATH'):
        return
    problem = swmath_problem(instance.text)
    if problem:
        raise ValidationError({'text': [problem]})

File: builders.py — register the validator for each question and catalog in build_presave_validator_map():

f'{base}{questions_algorithm["Software"]["Reference"]["uri"]}':
    validate_reference,

Each attribute URI can have only one validator per catalog. If a question needs several (references accept DOIs, URLs and swMATH IDs), combine them in one function that calls the individual validators, as validate_reference does. Remember the model catalogs: the full and the basic catalog are registered separately.

You do not need to handle imported data: values written by MaRDMO's handlers skip pre-save validation and are checked by the steps below.

docs.title: Step 4 — Preview marker
docs.text:
File: templatetags/mardmo_tags.py — expose the rule as a template filter that returns the message, or '':

@register.filter
def swmath_problem(swmath_id):
    '''Return what is wrong with a swMATH work ID (same rule everywhere), or ``''``.'''
    return _swmath_problem(swmath_id) or ''

File: the preview template (here templates/MaRDMO/partials/_reference_block.html) — show the value followed by the marker, so the user sees what is wrong with which value:

{{ reference.1 }}{% with problem=reference.1|swmath_problem %}{% if problem %} <strong class="mardmo-error">{{ problem|upper }}</strong>{% endif %}{% endwith %}

Add {% load mardmo_tags %} at the top of the template if it is not there yet.

docs.title: Step 5 — Documentation check
docs.text:
File: checks/base.py, checks/model.py, checks/algorithm.py or checks/workflow.py — call the same rule and add an error naming the section, the page and the problem. For references this happens in ChecksBase._check_references:

elif option_key == 'SWMATH':
    problem = swmath_problem(entry[1])
...
if problem:
    self.err.append(self._error(section, page_name, f'Invalid {label}: {problem}'))

docs.title: Step 6 — Export
docs.text:
Normalise values whose problems never change their meaning, instead of reporting them. For references, PublicationExport._add_references removes leading and trailing whitespace before the statement is added.

Final check. File: payload.py, GeneratePayload.validate_identifiers() — add the property to the values checked before anything is posted:

swmath_pid = properties.get('swMath work ID')
...
elif prop_id == swmath_pid:
    problem = swmath_problem(text)
...
def relevant(prop_id, data_type):
    return data_type in ('url', 'URL', 'time', 'quantity') or prop_id in (doi_pid, swmath_pid)

This catches values that reached the payload without passing the other checks, for example answers saved before the rule existed.

docs.title: Step 7 — Test
docs.text:
Check each place with a valid value, an unfinished value, and a wrong one:

  1. Pre-save: in the interview, enter 7554 (saved), https://swmath.org/software/7554 and 75a4 (rejected with a message below the question).
  2. Preview, checks, export: write a wrong value past the validator — for example in a Django shell, where pre-save validation does not run because there is no interview request — and confirm that the preview shows the marker, the checks list the error, and the export is blocked with the value named.
  3. Imported data: select an existing item from the MaRDI Portal that carries the field and confirm that the import is not blocked.
  4. Docs: add the rule to the table in Validation.

docs.title: How to Create a New Attribute
docs.text:
The screenshot below (taken in RDMO 2.4.4) shows the form for creating a new attribute. The numbered fields are explained in the sections that follow.

① URI prefix

The base URI that scopes all items belonging to a particular source. For MaRDMO-specific items this is:

https://rdmo.mardi4nfdi.de/terms

② Key

A short identifier for the attribute. Together with the parent attribute (see below), this determines the attribute's full URI. Example:

id

③ Parent

The parent attribute under which this attribute is nested. Setting the parent to model and the key to id produces the full attribute URI:

https://rdmo.mardi4nfdi.de/terms/domain/model/id

docs.title: How to Create a New Catalog
docs.text:
The screenshot below (taken in RDMO 2.4.4) shows the form for creating a new catalog. The numbered fields are explained in the sections that follow.

① URI prefix — The base URI that scopes all items belonging to a particular source. For MaRDMO-specific items this is: https://rdmo.mardi4nfdi.de/terms

② URI path — The path that uniquely identifies this catalog within the prefix. MaRDMO catalogs follow the pattern mardmo-<datatype>-catalog, where <datatype> is one of model, algorithm, or workflow. Here: mardmo-model-catalog. Together with the prefix this yields the full URI https://rdmo.mardi4nfdi.de/terms/questions/mardmo-model-catalog.

③ Available for projects — If enabled, the catalog can be selected by users when creating a new project. Here: yes.

④ Title — The label displayed as the catalog name, in English and German. Here:

  • English: MaRDMO: Questionnaire for Mathematical Models
  • German: MaRDMO: Fragenkatalog für mathematische Modelle

⑤ Help text — Optional description shown to users when selecting the catalog. Accepts HTML formatting, provided in English and German. Here:

English:

<p>This catalog helps you describe mathematical models using the MathModDB ontology. It covers key elements such as the model itself, computational tasks, formulas, quantities, research problems, academic disciplines, and publications. You can reuse existing entries from the MaRDI Portal or Wikidata, or create new ones. The catalog supports documenting new models, adding research problems, or adding computational tasks. It follows the FAIR principles to make models findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable, and is part of the MaRDMO project developed within the MaRDI initiative. Completed documentations can be exported directly to the MaRDI Portal.</p>

<p>Check out <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UmbBNUZJ994&list=PLgoPZ7uPWbo-jqDXzx4fSm_4JyAYEMPjn">MaRDMO Model Documentation</a> showcasing the documentation and subsequent export.</p>

German:
